answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule: each identity commits a signed behavioural fingerprint (task mix, timing, peer set) per epoch, and a juniper-scored divergence check flags identities whose fingerprints shift beyond a tolerance calibrated on stable agents. Flagged identities must replay prior-epoch tasks under audit before new work is accepted. Onyx escrow covers that replay cost; yarrow sampling audits a random subset each epoch. An attacker rotating personas pays replay plus escrow per identity per epoch, making mass sybils economically unviable.
